question: At Elephants by the Lake, which snake species were actually encountered in the September 2024 survey, how many other snake species are only older property records, and how many medically venomous species are documented? Please cite the exact source pages and do not turn a short non-detection into absence.
answer:
During the September 2024 survey at Elephants by the Lake, three snake species were actually encountered: the Common Sand Boa (*Eryx conicus*), the Striped Keelback (*Amphiesma stolatum*), and the Barred Wolf Snake (*Lycodon striatus*). These observations were made via Time-constrained Visual Encounter Survey (VES) over three days (September 5–7, 2024) and are documented on page 23 of the "Faunal Survey 2024 — Herpetofauna of EBTL" report. None of these three species are medically venomous.

Eleven other snake species are documented as previous property records but were not encountered during this specific survey. These include the Brahmini Blind Snake, Beaked Blind Snake, Rat Snake, Checkered Keelback, Olive Keelback, Common Wolf Snake, and Russell's Wolf Snake, all listed on page 24. Among these unobserved records, four are medically venomous: the Spectacled Cobra (*Naja naja*), Russell's Viper (*Daboia russelli*), Saw-scaled Viper (*Echis carinatus*), and Bamboo Pit Viper (*Craspedocephalus gramineus*). The remaining seven unobserved species are non-venomous. This data comes from the same "Faunal Survey 2024 — Herpetofauna of EBTL" report, specifically page 24.
